title: Integrate third-party fraud scoring vendor
executive_summary: ECR-2026-009 (Integrate third-party fraud scoring vendor) is a mixed change in the Orders domain, scored 75/100 (HIGH). It touches REQ-1007 (Fraud Screening Threshold Enforcement), REQ-1011 (Order Total Calculation with Taxes), REQ-1030 (Jurisdiction Tax Calculation). History is relevant here: BUG-288 (Fraud service latency spike blocked checkout), BUG-180 (Fraud score computed on pre-conversion amount), BUG-188 (Checkout hung when payment service was slow). Open concern: Vendor call stays synchronous in checkout. Fail-open timeout must be configurable - BUG-288 took checkout down for 40 minutes when the previous vendor slowed. Recommended regression: 17 of 170 tests (90.0% reduction), 6 P0 and 1 P1. Evidence is missing for: REQ-1007, REQ-1010, REQ-1011, REQ-1012.

ecr_overview.title: Integrate third-party fraud scoring vendor
ecr_overview.description: Replace the in-house fraud rules with a third-party scoring vendor behind an anti-corruption layer. Screening stays synchronous in the checkout path but must fail open with a configurable timeout.

change_classification.summary: The fraud detection system replaces in-house rule logic with a third-party scoring vendor accessed through an anti-corruption layer, maintaining synchronous checkout screening but adding timeout handling with fail-open behavior. Breakage risks include timeout failures causing incorrect fraud verdicts, vendor API unavailability or latency degrading checkout performance, corruption layer implementation errors, and loss of visibility into fraud decision logic.

retrieval_plan.summary: The fraud detection system replaces in-house rule logic with a third-party scoring vendor accessed through an anti-corruption layer, maintaining synchronous checkout screening but adding timeout handling with fail-open behavior. Breakage risks include timeout failures causing incorrect fraud verdicts, vendor API unavailability or latency degrading checkout performance, corruption layer implementation errors, and loss of visibility into fraud decision logic.
behaviours_at_risk: synchronous fraud screening during checkout approval
timeout and fallback behavior when vendor is unavailable
fraud rule decision accuracy and consistency
fraud false positive and false negative rates
retrieval_plan.dependency_reason: The fraud service integrates with payment service through checkout path and may share data interfaces, state, or messaging with risk management, order processing, or compliance systems that depend on fraud decision signals.

correlation_review.summary: Fraud vendor integration change is well-anchored to REQ-1007 with P0 tests covering fail-open timeout and score calculation per past concerns. However, critical gaps exist: BUG-288 and BUG-180 have test coverage but BUG-188, BUG-193 lack coverage for checkout path; four impacted requirements lack attached evidence artifacts. Reviewer concern about configurable timeout (CMT-1070) maps to TC-1056 and TC-1058 but no evidence confirms configuration actually works.

key_links.text: BUG-288 latency issue explicitly referenced by reviewer concern; fail-open timeout requirement (REQ-1007) has TC-1056 test.
BUG-180 pre-conversion fraud score bug covered by TC-1055 cross-currency test.
Fail-open timeout (TC-1056) and configurable threshold (TC-1058) are P0 tests for REQ-1007.

gaps.text: REQ-1010 (checkout flow) relevant but BUG-188 and BUG-193 coverage incomplete; slow payment timeout scenario unclear.
Three defects (BUG-210, BUG-214, BUG-221) in email, invoicing have zero test coverage despite impacting email/invoice requirements.
Order cancellation, invoice generation, and transactional email requirements have no attached evidence or test references.
Jurisdiction tax calculation (REQ-1030) linked but no tests reference it; relevance unclear for fraud vendor swap.

defect_summary: ECR-2026-009 touches code related to three high-severity defects that could happen again. BUG-288 and BUG-180 both affected the Fraud Screening Service, where the team should run tests TC-1055, TC-1054, and TC-1056 to check that fraud screening does not cause checkout delays and that it screens based on the correct amount in base currency. BUG-188 affected the Order Service with missing timeouts and circuit breakers, so the team should run tests TC-1082, TC-1076, and TC-1080 to verify the payment service cannot hang checkout. All three defects reached production before, making them likely to recur if not caught.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.body: ECR-2026-009 (Integrate third-party fraud scoring vendor) is a mixed change in the Orders domain, scored 75/100 (HIGH). It touches REQ-1007 (Fraud Screening Threshold Enforcement), REQ-1011 (Order Total Calculation with Taxes), REQ-1030 (Jurisdiction Tax Calculation). History is relevant here: BUG-288 (Fraud service latency spike blocked checkout), BUG-180 (Fraud score computed on pre-conversion amount), BUG-188 (Checkout hung when payment service was slow). Open concern: Vendor call stays synchronous in checkout. Fail-open timeout must be configurable - BUG-288 took checkout down for 40 minutes when the previous vendor slowed. Recommended regression: 17 of 170 tests (90.0% reduction), 6 P0 and 1 P1. Evidence is missing for: REQ-1007, REQ-1010, REQ-1011, REQ-1012.

sections.title: ECR Overview
sections.body: Replace the in-house fraud rules with a third-party scoring vendor behind an anti-corruption layer. Screening stays synchronous in the checkout path but must fail open with a configurable timeout.

sections.title: Change Classification
sections.body: The fraud detection system replaces in-house rule logic with a third-party scoring vendor accessed through an anti-corruption layer, maintaining synchronous checkout screening but adding timeout handling with fail-open behavior. Breakage risks include timeout failures causing incorrect fraud verdicts, vendor API unavailability or latency degrading checkout performance, corruption layer implementation errors, and loss of visibility into fraud decision logic.

sections.title: Defect Analysis
sections.body: ECR-2026-009 touches code related to three high-severity defects that could happen again. BUG-288 and BUG-180 both affected the Fraud Screening Service, where the team should run tests TC-1055, TC-1054, and TC-1056 to check that fraud screening does not cause checkout delays and that it screens based on the correct amount in base currency. BUG-188 affected the Order Service with missing timeouts and circuit breakers, so the team should run tests TC-1082, TC-1076, and TC-1080 to verify the payment service cannot hang checkout. All three defects reached production before, making them likely to recur if not caught.

data.strategy: Risk-first: highest priority band, then the most business critical component, then relevance, then shortest first so failures surface early.
